text: Nature supplies the picture — and mark that this step is an observation, not a verse: milk is food another body has already digested; the infant does no work, it swallows what was broken down for it, and grows.
Now go back to the synagogue at Capernaum, where this book began — and notice that Jesus began with sym:sym-bread[bread].

Mark that distinction, because the common teaching runs exactly backwards.
Stop and weigh that rebuke.
Close the Gospels; what could a hearer of Moses and the prophets make of that?
Now derive what the thorns *mean*, for the Old Testament assigns that too.

Disciples do forsake all — Peter says so five verses later and is not corrected (Matthew 19:27), and __“whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple”__ (Luke 14:33) — but mark what no disciple ever did: buy the field.
And mark why the score was owed: not one answer hung on a single verse.

Where He supplied none — the mustard tree, the leaven, the treasure, the pearl — the same Scriptures carry the reader most of the way, and mark plainly where the derivation ends and the testing begins.

The King James’ __“ensamples”__ is the Greek _typos_ — types, patterns struck in advance — and mark the two verbs: the things __“happened”__ as types before they were __“written”__ as types (so too 1 Corinthians 10:6).
But watch what Scripture calls a sign, and notice that there is no wonder in it anywhere.

But mark what happened on the day the sign was given: nothing.

And mark the double truth in the verbs: Jonah offers himself — __“cast me forth”__ — yet it is other hands that take him up and cast him; exactly as the Messiah is __“delivered… by wicked hands”__ (Acts 2:23) and yet insists, __“No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself”__ (John 10:18).
Notice that God, answering, plays on David’s own word — for a __“house”__ in Scripture is a building _and_ a family line, and a family line is exactly what carries a name.
Mark that sentence, because it is the Bible’s standing formula for a deposed covenant partner.

And mark that the trap was lawless on its face: the statute they quoted requires *both* — __“they shall *both* of them die, both the *man* that lay with the woman, and the woman”__ (Deuteronomy 22:22; Leviticus 20:10) — and a woman taken in the very act was taken with a man they knew and did not bring.
Weigh the chapter the way the evidence is built.
And mark where the ratio lives: in the very verse where the divorced wife is called home — __“for I am married unto you,”__ the remarriage of the sym:sym-marriage[marriage] chapter.
The most demonstratively religious one percent was not enough — hold that word __“exceed”__; the Hebrew of the remnant will hand it back to us shortly.

Offered the open sky, the servant chooses the house — for sym:sym-love[love], which Scripture defines as keeping the master’s commandments — and mark where and how the choice is sealed: his *ear*, at the *door post*.
Now consider the first time the word appears in the Bible, because Scripture’s first use of a word is a teacher.

Before weighing the evidence, weigh the witnesses, for Scripture itself commands it.

And mark who waits at the corners: on the garment, the corner is where the law hangs its reminder — __“that ye may look upon it, and *remember all the commandments* of the LORD”__ (Numbers 15:39) — and at the earth's four wings wait __“the remnant… which *keep the commandments* of God”__ (Revelation 12:17).
And mark where the scene stands: after the sixth seal is opened (Revelation 6:12) — the riders commissioned at the first four seals are still reined in at the four corners when the sixth is broken.
And mark what an almond *is*: a fruit that is itself a sym:sym-seed[seed] — and __“the seed is the *word of God*”__ (Luke 8:11).

Notice that this is the very same chapter that defined the mountain (Revelation 17:9-10).
And mark the third symbol: the hidden thing is *swords*, and the sword is the word — __“the sword of the Spirit, which is the *word of God*”__ (Ephesians 6:17).
Taste what is set before you, and mark whether it was churned — or merely smoothed.
And __“lest they trample”__ reads __“lest they *chew* them”__ — and mark that verb: _karsam_ stands exactly *once* in the whole Hebrew Bible, at the boar in Asaph's vine.

[[sym-coin]]Coin verdict:novel[]:: The stamped image — a person as the owner's minted image-bearer: dug from the sym:sym-field[field], refined in the fire, struck with the sym:sym-name[NAME]; priced by the law, ransomed at a flat half-shekel when counted, lost and sought by sym:sym-lamp[lamplight]. Man's mint valued the Shepherd at slave-damages; God's scales weigh the sym:sym-widow[widow]'s whole living above all abundance. +
